about: Reranker corpus: score (request, tool description) pairs. Generated by tools/build_reranker_corpus.py, seed 20261013. Negatives come from the selector's own top-12, not from uniform sampling - the tools that crowd out the answer are the ones it already rates highest.
limit: Evidence for tool RANKING, and for arguments on the 111 of 220 cases that carry them. `ascension_gate` scores right tool AND right arguments, so a run graded by it is answerable on 111 rows and NOT on the 109 with no arguments - a verdict drawn from those 111 is a verdict about argument-bearing requests and says nothing about the rest.

train.say: Clear the cache folder you said was taking the space.
train.positives_desc: cleanup_apply: Actually free the disk space cleanup_report measured: empty your cache folder, or remove Flatpak runtimes no app uses. Both are recoverable or provably unused. Requires the 'cleanup-enabled' consent key. The system log is not here - that needs root, which Chronoa cannot ask for from inside a tool call. (arguments: target)

negatives.desc: space_by_type: Break disk usage down by kind of file - video, audio, image, document, archive, code and so on - across all directories, rather than per directory. Use for 'what is eating my disk', 'is it the photos or the documents', 'what takes up the space in here'. Names the largest category, and reports files whose type it could not tell as a visible `other` bucket rather than dropping them. Read-only. (arguments: path)

list_directory: List the files and folders in a directory, with each one's type and size. Use this to see what is in a folder before opening, moving or deleting anything in it. (arguments: path, include_hidden)

directory_tree: Show the shape of a directory as a nested tree, with each entry's type. Use this to understand how a project or folder is laid out before opening files in it. Reports what it skipped and when it stopped early. (arguments: path, max_depth, include_hidden)

empty_directories: Find directories under a path that hold nothing at all. Use for 'clean up empty folders', 'what are these leftover directories', 'tidy this up'. Empty means rmdir would succeed - a directory holding only sub-directories is not empty - and one that cannot be read is not empty either. Reports what it found and removes nothing. Read-only. (arguments: path, limit)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

sync_folder: Sync one folder to another, sending only what changed - and show the plan first, before anything is copied. Use for 'copy my files to the server', 'sync these folders', 'what would change if I synced'. Does not delete anything at the destination unless you ask it to, and asks first even then. (arguments: source, destination, apply, delete)

todo_list: Keep a list of tasks that survives between turns and restarts: add an item, change its status, mark what it is blocked by, or list what is outstanding. Use this to track a multi-step job rather than holding it in the conversation. Requires the 'todo-list-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, id, content, status, blocked_by)

train.say: Where this computer is.
train.positives_desc: get_location: Where this computer is right now - latitude, longitude and accuracy - from a GPS receiver or GNOME's location service. Use for 'where am I'. Requires the location sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off.

negatives.desc: bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)
data_usage: How much internet data this computer has used today and this month, per network interface (from vnStat).

disk_activity: How hard this machine's disks are working right now: reads and writes per second, average wait, and how much of each disk's time is spent busy. Answers 'why is my computer slow', 'why is the disk grinding', 'is something writing all the time'. Read-only; nothing is started or stopped.

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': what the pairing half of the protocol is and why it is not here. Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

login_history: Recent logins to this machine: which user, from which terminal or remote address, when they started and how long they lasted, and recent reboots. Use for 'who logged in', 'has anyone used my computer'. Requires the 'sessions-sense-enabled' consent key, because it reports other people's presence. Read-only. (arguments: limit)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

train.say: List the lab networks built on this machine.
train.positives_desc: lab_network_list: List the isolated lab networks built on this machine, with their subnets. Read-only.

negatives.desc: lab_network_destroy: Remove a lab network built by lab_network_create, and everything in it. Only ever removes networks this tool built. Returns the plan unless apply=true. (arguments: name, apply)

lab_network_create: Build an isolated lab network on this machine: a network namespace holding a bridge, with named subnets in namespaces of their own. A public subnet can reach the internet through the uplink; a private one can reach this network and nothing beyond it. Returns the exact plan and changes nothing unless apply=true, which needs your system password. (arguments: name, cidr, subnets, internet, apply)
lab_network_status: What a lab network can actually reach: a real ping from inside each subnet, not just what the routing table says. (arguments: name)

list_wifi_networks: Scan for and list the WiFi networks in range, with signal strength and whether this machine is joined to one. Scans the radio, so it requires the 'network-sense-enabled' consent. (arguments: rescan)

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.

network_activity: Report what this machine's network is doing right now, per program: which processes are sending and receiving, and how fast each interface is moving. Use for 'what is using my bandwidth', 'why is the network slow', 'what is uploading', 'is something downloading right now'. Interface rates come from /proc/net/dev and always work; per-program rates need nethogs and can only name programs this user owns. Says which half it could not measure and why, and reports an unattributed socket as unattributed rather than guessing at a program. Read-only; nothing is changed or blocked.

scan_network: Find which devices are on the local network, with their names, addresses and hardware vendors. Local addresses only. Requires the network sense to be enabled. (arguments: range, resolve_names)

train.say: start a new conversation
train.positives_desc: conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

negatives.desc: open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

train.say: Mute the microphone, disable a camera, or blank the screen.
train.positives_desc: set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

negatives.desc: set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)
set_mute: Mute or unmute the sound from the speakers or headphones ('mute the sound', 'unmute'). The microphone is set_mic_mute. (arguments: mute, device)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

lock_screen: Lock this session so a password is needed to come back to it. Uses the session's own mechanism so the same thing happens as the desktop's Lock button. Requires the 'screen-lock-enabled' consent key.

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

train.say: search the web for the latest news about ISRO
train.positives_desc: web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

negatives.desc: news: News headlines only (title, source, age), from Google News (or BBC) RSS feeds - not facts or what a page says, which is web_search. With no topic: the top stories. A topic can be a section - world, business, tech, science, health, sports, entertainment - or anything to search for, e.g. 'ISRO'. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: topic, source, limit)

search_my_files: Search your own files by meaning - documents, notes, code - in a directory you choose, or your home if you name none. 'search': what matches a few words. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh the index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, path, limit)

search_documents: Search inside the user's files by their contents, using the desktop's own search index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). Requires the 'document-search-enabled' consent key. (arguments: query, kind, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

train.say: Virtual machines.
train.positives_desc: list_vms: List the virtual machines defined with libvirt - both your own (GNOME Boxes) and the system-wide ones (virt-manager) - and whether each is running, paused or shut off. Use for 'what VMs do I have', 'is my Windows VM running'. Read-only.

negatives.desc: vm: Run a virtual machine with QEMU and drive it like a browser: launch it with a visible window on the desktop and a QMP control socket beside it, photograph its screen, send key combinations, type text into it, move and click its pointer (percentages of its screen), check its power state, and stop it. Requires the 'vm-control-enabled' consent key, off by default. Listing the VMs already running is `list_vms` (virsh) or this skill's list action; this one starts and drives them. (arguments: action, name, memory_mb, iso, disk, display, firmware, tpm, keys, text, x, y, button)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

train.say: open firefox
train.positives_desc: open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

negatives.desc: open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

train.say: Who is on this network right now.
train.positives_desc: discover_hosts: Find which devices are on this network right now, by asking rather than by reading the cache - so devices that have never talked to this machine are found too. Reports an address and a hardware address for each, and counts devices answering on more than one address. The range is always the private network this machine is on; pass network= for a different private range, and a public one is refused. Connects to nothing it finds and reads no packet contents. Needs raw-socket access, so unprivileged it may report that rather than a partial sweep. (arguments: interface, network)

negatives.desc: lookup_wikipedia: Who or what something is - a person, place, thing or event - from Wikipedia's summary. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: topic)

network_activity: Report what this machine's network is doing right now, per program: which processes are sending and receiving, and how fast each interface is moving. Use for 'what is using my bandwidth', 'why is the network slow', 'what is uploading', 'is something downloading right now'. Says which half it could not measure and why, and reports an unattributed socket as unattributed rather than guessing at a program. Read-only; nothing is changed or blocked.
lab_network_list: List the isolated lab networks built on this machine, with their subnets. Read-only.

lab_network_create: Build an isolated lab network on this machine: a network namespace holding a bridge, with named subnets in namespaces of their own. A public subnet can reach the internet through the uplink; a private one can reach this network and nothing beyond it. Returns the exact plan and changes nothing unless apply=true, which needs your system password. (arguments: name, cidr, subnets, internet, apply)
lab_network_destroy: Remove a lab network built by lab_network_create, and everything in it. Only ever removes networks this tool built. Returns the plan unless apply=true. (arguments: name, apply)
lab_network_status: What a lab network can actually reach: a real ping from inside each subnet, not just what the routing table says. (arguments: name)

list_wifi_networks: Scan for and list the WiFi networks in range, with signal strength and whether this machine is joined to one. Scans the radio, so it requires the 'network-sense-enabled' consent. (arguments: rescan)

scan_network: Find which devices are on the local network, with their names, addresses and hardware vendors. Local addresses only. Requires the network sense to be enabled. (arguments: range, resolve_names)

train.say: What changed in a git repository.
train.positives_desc: git_inspect: Report a git working tree: what has changed and is not committed, the diff of those changes, recent commits, or the current branch and how far it is from its upstream; also the stashed work and the reflog (the record that survives rebases and amends). Reports UNKNOWN - never 'clean tree' - when git is missing, the folder is not a repository, or git fails. Requires the 'git-sense-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, subcommand, revision, since, context_lines)

negatives.desc: git_push: Push a branch to a named remote. Requires the 'git-push-enabled' consent key, and asks before every push. The remote must be one the repository already has, and must be named - there is no default and no 'push everything'. Force-pushing is refused. (arguments: remote, branch, set_upstream, path)

git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)
git_branch: Create a branch in a git repository and switch to it, or switch to a branch that already exists. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. (arguments: name, path)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

vcs_status: What state a checkout is in, for git, subversion or mercurial: which version control system it belongs to, the branch or revision, the repository it points at, and what has changed. Use when the answer might not be git - 'what is this folder's state', 'which repository is this', 'what changed in my checkout'. Read-only; runs nothing that modifies a repository. (arguments: path)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

undo_last_change: Put a file back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content recorded just before Chronoa's own last edit to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, steps)

train.say: Open blaze demo dot com and find the cheapest flight from Boston to London.
train.positives_desc: browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

negatives.desc: web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

search_documents: Search inside the user's files by their contents, using the desktop's own search index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). Requires the 'document-search-enabled' consent key. (arguments: query, kind, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

train.say: Steps, sleep, stress, heart rate, SpO2 and settings on your watch.
train.positives_desc: watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

negatives.desc: power_action: Suspend (sleep), hibernate, restart or shut down this computer, or cancel a scheduled restart/shutdown. Restart and shutdown happen after one minute and can be cancelled. Requires the 'power-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

set_sleep_inhibit: Report what is currently holding the machine awake, or take a bounded hold so it does not sleep for a while, or release ours. Use for 'keep it awake while I...' - a long install, a backup, a test run. Scoped and self-lapsing; to change the machine's idle timeout permanently use set_screensaver instead. Gated by 'sleep-inhibit-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, reason, seconds)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

set_power_profile: Switch the machine between its power profiles - typically power-saver, balanced and performance - and report which one is active now. The profile list is read from the machine rather than assumed, because which profiles exist depends on the CPU driver: switching to one the machine does not have is refused with the valid names listed. Changes the CPU and platform power behaviour, not a per-application setting. (arguments: profile)

calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

train.say: This computer's name.
train.positives_desc: set_hostname: Report this computer's name (hostname), or rename it - the name other devices on the network and in Bluetooth see. The name must be letters, digits and hyphens only. Renaming requires the 'hostname-control-enabled' consent key and the administrator password; reporting needs neither. (arguments: action, name)

negatives.desc: files_by_name: Find every file with a given name under a directory, with sizes and modification dates, so you can see whether they are copies. Use for 'where are all my report.docx', 'how many copies of this do I have', 'which is the newest'. Reports the newest and whether the sizes agree, and does NOT claim the contents match - duplicate_files answers that. Deletes nothing. (arguments: name, path, case_sensitive)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)
data_usage: How much internet data this computer has used today and this month, per network interface (from vnStat).

disk_activity: How hard this machine's disks are working right now: reads and writes per second, average wait, and how much of each disk's time is spent busy. Answers 'why is my computer slow', 'why is the disk grinding', 'is something writing all the time'. Read-only; nothing is started or stopped.

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': what the pairing half of the protocol is and why it is not here. Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

train.say: Can this machine roll back, and which slot is it on.
train.positives_desc: snapshot_status: Whether this Shanios machine can roll back: the OS version, which blue/green slot was booted, which slot boots next, the previous slot a rollback would return to, any recorded boot failure or pending reboot, and the btrfs snapshots on disk. Use for 'can I undo the update', 'which slot am I on', 'is an update waiting'. The snapshot list uses the 'snapshots-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

negatives.desc: random_pick: Flip a coin, roll dice ('2d6'), pick a random number in a range, or choose one of a list of options. (arguments: kind, dice, low, high, options)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

backup_status: Whether this machine's files are actually backed up off it: how many restic snapshots exist, when the most recent was taken, what it covered, and whether the repository still passes restic's own integrity check. Use for 'is my backup working', 'when did I last back up', 'do I have a copy of my files'. A machine with no repository configured says so plainly, because that means there is no backup. Read-only: it never writes to the repository. (arguments: repository)

dns_lookup: Look a hostname or address up in DNS and report what came back: the addresses, or the mail servers, name servers, TXT records, certificate records or other records a name publishes, and whether the answer is DNSSEC-signed and valid. Distinguishes 'this name does not exist' from 'the resolver did not answer', because those have different fixes. Obeys privacy mode, since the query goes to a resolver outside this machine. Read-only. (arguments: name, type)

driver_build: Build a scaffolded out-of-tree kernel module with Kbuild, then read the resulting .ko back off disk. Needs the 'driver-build-enabled' consent key. Refuses with the missing package named when this machine has no toolchain. (arguments: name, path)

train.say: make a QR code for https://shani.dev
train.positives_desc: qr_code: read: decode every QR code and barcode in a picture (path) or on the screen (screen=true, needs the vision consent). create: make a QR code PNG of text (a URL, Wi-Fi details, a note) at output. (arguments: action, path, screen, text, output)

negatives.desc: solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

capture_video: Record a short video from the camera (webcam), e.g. '/dev/video0', for a few seconds. Requires the vision/camera consent. Writes a new .mp4; no camera means a clear refusal. (arguments: device, seconds, infrared)

manage_mount: Mount an unmounted filesystem or drive, or unmount one, through the desktop's own disk service so its authorisation rules apply. Verifies the result against the mount table. Requires the 'mount-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device)

network_activity: Report what this machine's network is doing right now, per program: which processes are sending and receiving, and how fast each interface is moving. Use for 'what is using my bandwidth', 'why is the network slow', 'what is uploading', 'is something downloading right now'. Interface rates come from /proc/net/dev and always work; per-program rates need nethogs and can only name programs this user owns. Says which half it could not measure and why, and reports an unattributed socket as unattributed rather than guessing at a program. Read-only; nothing is changed or blocked.

set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

train.say: Stop a process.
train.positives_desc: kill_process: Stop a running process by pid, asking it to exit cleanly. Use list_processes to find the pid first. Requires the 'process-kill-enabled' consent key. (arguments: pid, signal_name)

negatives.desc: process_cost: What each running program is COSTING this machine right now, measured over the last second rather than as a snapshot: percent CPU split into user and system time, how much memory it holds, page faults (including the major ones that mean it is thrashing), and how many kB a second it is reading and writing. Answers 'what is using my CPU', 'what is making my computer slow', 'what is writing to my disk all the time', 'which program is swapping', 'why did everything freeze'. Use this when the machine feels slow; use list_processes to see what is running and disk_activity to see whether the disk itself is busy. Read-only; nothing is started, stopped or changed.

process_detail: What one running process is doing right now: its state (running, sleeping, stopped, zombie), and the kernel function it is waiting on if it is blocked. Answers 'why is that window frozen', 'what is this program stuck on', 'is this process hung'. Read-only: it attaches to nothing, runs nothing, and never needs root for your own processes. (arguments: pid)

cpu_per_core: Which individual processor cores are busy right now, and how much of each is user time versus waiting on disk. Use when the machine feels slow but nothing looks busy - a single process pinning one core looks idle in every system-wide average. Read-only; starts nothing.

oom_score: Which process the kernel would kill if memory ran out, and whether it has killed anything already. Reports how much time this machine has spent stalled waiting on memory, the kernel's own ranking of who would go first, any process somebody deliberately marked as more expendable, and how many processes the kernel has OOM-killed since boot. Answers 'who would the kernel kill', 'why did my program disappear', 'is my machine short on memory', 'has anything been killed', 'what would happen if I opened more'. Use this when something vanished or the machine stalled; use list_processes to see what is running and the memory sense to see how much is used. Read-only; nothing is adjusted and nothing is killed.

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)
port_owner: Find which program is using a network port, or list what this machine is listening on and connected to. Read-only. (arguments: port, process, kind, listening, limit)

thread_activity: Show the individual THREADS of a process - or of the whole machine - with the CPU each is using right now and the kernel function it is blocked in. Use for 'which thread is using the CPU', 'this program is at 300 percent', 'what is this thread waiting on', 'why is this stuck', 'which of these threads is busy'. Goes one level below process_detail and list_processes, which report one figure for the whole process and cannot tell a program with one hot thread from one using every core evenly. Read-only; nothing is sampled with a tool, attached to or changed. (arguments: pid)

train.say: Build an isolated lab network with named subnets.
train.positives_desc: lab_network_create: Build an isolated lab network on this machine: a network namespace holding a bridge, with named subnets in namespaces of their own. A public subnet can reach the internet through the uplink; a private one can reach this network and nothing beyond it. Returns the exact plan and changes nothing unless apply=true, which needs your system password. (arguments: name, cidr, subnets, internet, apply)

negatives.desc: lab_network_list: List the isolated lab networks built on this machine, with their subnets. Read-only.
lab_network_status: What a lab network can actually reach: a real ping from inside each subnet, not just what the routing table says. (arguments: name)
lab_network_destroy: Remove a lab network built by lab_network_create, and everything in it. Only ever removes networks this tool built. Returns the plan unless apply=true. (arguments: name, apply)

driver_build: Build a scaffolded out-of-tree kernel module with Kbuild, then read the resulting .ko back off disk. Needs the 'driver-build-enabled' consent key. Refuses with the missing package named when this machine has no toolchain. (arguments: name, path)

scan_network: Find which devices are on the local network, with their names, addresses and hardware vendors. Local addresses only. Requires the network sense to be enabled. (arguments: range, resolve_names)

list_wifi_networks: Scan for and list the WiFi networks in range, with signal strength and whether this machine is joined to one. Scans the radio, so it requires the 'network-sense-enabled' consent. (arguments: rescan)

network_activity: Report what this machine's network is doing right now, per program: which processes are sending and receiving, and how fast each interface is moving. Use for 'what is using my bandwidth', 'why is the network slow', 'what is uploading', 'is something downloading right now'. Interface rates come from /proc/net/dev and always work; per-program rates need nethogs and can only name programs this user owns. Says which half it could not measure and why, and reports an unattributed socket as unattributed rather than guessing at a program. Read-only; nothing is changed or blocked.

train.say: Remind me tomorrow at 9 to pack my bags.
train.positives_desc: reminders: A dated list of reminders you can keep coming back to: add one, list what is still due, mark one done, or remove one. Optionally with a due time in words, e.g. 'tomorrow 9am' or 'in 3 hours'. (arguments: action, number, text, due)

negatives.desc: calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

date_math: Date arithmetic: days until a date ('how many days until 25 December'), the date N days/weeks/months from a date ('what date is 45 days from now'), days between two dates, or the weekday of a date. (arguments: operation, date, other_date, amount, unit)

get_weather: Current weather and today's forecast - temperature, feels-like, rain, wind - for a named place, or for where this computer is if no place is given; with `when`, the forecast for tomorrow, a weekday, this week or the weekend instead. Use for weather, temperature outside, rain, forecast. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: place, when)

train.say: Run ls inside my web container.
train.positives_desc: container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

negatives.desc: list_containers: List this machine's containers: distroboxes (by name, with their image and whether they are running) and podman/docker containers, including any that exited because they ran out of memory, plus how much disk the images use. Use for 'what distroboxes do I have', 'is my container running', 'why did my container die'. The podman details use the 'containers-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

explain_command: Explain a Linux shell command (not a general topic) from the local manuals (tldr, man), e.g. 'what does tar do', 'how do I use rsync'; or find which command does something, e.g. 'which command shows disk usage'. (arguments: command, task)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. train.say: Report the radios, or turn airplane mode on or off.
train.positives_desc: airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

negatives.desc: toggle_wifi: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off (only Wi-Fi - airplane_mode switches every radio, connect_wifi joins a network), or report whether Wi-Fi is on. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key; status needs no permission. (arguments: action)

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

toggle_bluetooth: Turn the Bluetooth adapter on or off, or report its state and the paired devices. Requires the 'bluetooth-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

toggle_night_light: Report or turn on/off the blue-light filter (GNOME night light), reporting the schedule separately from the on/off state, because a filter that is enabled with its schedule off is not currently doing anything. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

train.say: Battery, screenshot, apps and files of a phone connected with adb.
train.positives_desc: android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

negatives.desc: phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': what the pairing half of the protocol is and why it is not here. Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)
screenshot: Capture the screen to a PNG file and return the path it was saved to. Refuses when there is no display.

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results)

search_documents: Search inside the user's files by their contents, using the desktop's own search index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). Requires the 'document-search-enabled' consent key. (arguments: query, kind, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

search_my_files: Search your own files by meaning - documents, notes, code - in a directory you choose, or your home if you name none. 'search': what matches a few words. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh the index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, path, limit)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

train.say: Merge, split or take pages out of PDFs.
train.positives_desc: pdf_pages: Work with PDF pages without re-rendering them: 'info' (page count), 'merge' several PDFs into one (paths, in order), 'split' a PDF into one file per page (into a folder), or 'extract' some pages (e.g. '1-3,7') into a new PDF. Always writes new files; never overwrites an existing one or changes the originals. No rotation. (arguments: action, path, paths, pages, output)

negatives.desc: take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

boot_report: How the last boot went: total boot time split into firmware, loader, kernel and userspace, the services that took longest to start, when the machine booted and whether it shut down cleanly before, and which EFI entry the firmware will boot by default. Use for 'why does it boot slowly', 'did it crash last time'. Boot history uses the 'boots-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only. (arguments: top)

process_cost: What each running program is COSTING this machine right now, measured over the last second rather than as a snapshot: percent CPU split into user and system time, how much memory it holds, page faults (including the major ones that mean it is thrashing), and how many kB a second it is reading and writing. Answers 'what is using my CPU', 'what is making my computer slow', 'what is writing to my disk all the time', 'which program is swapping', 'why did everything freeze'. Use this when the machine feels slow; use list_processes to see what is running and disk_activity to see whether the disk itself is busy. Read-only; nothing is started, stopped or changed.

apply_patch: Apply a .patch or .diff file to files on this machine. Use for 'apply this diff', 'here is a patch', 'merge this change in'. Runs a dry run by default and changes nothing until asked.
