(arguments: patch, path, strip, action)

train.say: Focus a window.
train.positives_desc: focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

negatives.desc: close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

arrange_window: Minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send a window to another workspace, by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. move takes x and y, resize takes width and height (pixels), set_workspace takes a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace)

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

list_apps: List the applications installed on this machine, optionally filtered by a search term, so a request to open something can be answered with what actually exists rather than a guess. (arguments: search)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

train.say: Trim, normalize, change volume or speed.

End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

negatives.desc: speed_test: Measure this internet connection: latency, download speed and upload speed, against Cloudflare's speed-test servers. edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. (arguments: device)
set_volume: Set the system output volume to an exact percentage. (arguments: percent, device)

(arguments: path, list, steps)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. The whole folder goes as one item and can be restored from the trash - nothing in this project is deleted permanently, so there is no faster or 'real' delete to reach for instead. Requires the 'file-delete-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path)

train.say: Listen to FM radio through a USB receiver.
train.positives_desc: fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

negatives.desc: usb_devices: What is plugged into this machine's USB ports (mice, phones, webcams, sticks, with their speed), and every Thunderbolt/USB4 device with whether it is authorised to work. Use for 'what's plugged in', 'why doesn't my dock work', 'is my webcam connected'. The USB list uses the 'usb-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

get_location: Where this computer is right now - latitude, longitude and accuracy - from a GPS receiver or GNOME's location service. Use for 'where am I'. Requires the location sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off.

airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

negatives.desc: lookup_wikipedia: Who or what something is - a person, place, thing or event - from Wikipedia's summary. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: topic)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. search_documents: Search inside the user's files by their contents, using the desktop's own search index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). Requires the 'document-search-enabled' consent key. (arguments: query, kind, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

cloud_files: See what is in this machine's configured cloud storage remotes - which remotes rclone knows, how many objects and bytes each holds, and what is at the top level of one. Use for 'what is in my cloud drive', 'is anything in the bucket', 'how big is my remote'. Read-only: it never copies, syncs or deletes anything. A machine with no remotes says so, because that means there is nowhere off-machine for anything to go. (arguments: remote, path)

train.say: When, where and with what camera a photo was taken.
train.positives_desc: photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

set_wallpaper: Report or change the GNOME desktop wallpaper, setting the light and dark variants together. Refuses a path that does not exist, rather than leaving a blank desktop with no error. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, image)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. Saves a PNG and returns its path. (arguments: prompt, avoid, size, steps, seed, output, from_photo, strength)

photos: Find the user's photos by what is in them or written on them, or when they were taken. search: query like 'receipt hardware shop', 'dog on the beach', 'december 2025'; index: update the index of the Pictures folder (a batch at a time); status: how much is indexed. (arguments: action, query, captions)

take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

train.say: Read a video's length, size, and format.
train.positives_desc: read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

negatives.desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

(arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

create_directory: Create a directory, and any missing parent directories. Succeeds without complaint if it already exists. (arguments: path)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reports the applied theme separately from the preference, because setting the preference does not make every application follow it. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

train.say: Start or stop a service.
train.positives_desc: control_service: Start, stop, restart, reload, enable or disable a system service, then read its state back so the reply says whether it actually came up. Requires the 'service-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: unit, action)

negatives.desc: open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

check_units: Check whether systemd unit files are valid and say what is wrong with them - a missing ExecStart binary, an unknown key, a dependency that does not exist - by running systemd-analyze verify on just the units you name. With no unit named, lists the services this machine has. This is a static check of the file: it does not know whether a dependency is down or a path is mounted, so a clean report does not promise the service will start. Reading only; nothing is started, stopped or changed. (arguments: unit)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)
stopwatch: A stopwatch: start, lap, read the time so far, or stop. (arguments: action)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

train.say: The machine's routing table.
train.positives_desc: routing_table: Show this machine's routing table: which interface traffic leaves by, which router forwards it, and for IPv4 and IPv6 separately. Read-only, and changes nothing. (arguments: family, interface)

negatives.desc: neighbour_table: Show the neighbour (ARP) table for this machine: which addresses on this link have answered, which have never answered and are holding packets instead of sending them, and which have gone stale. That distinction is the one layer 3 cannot make - an unresolved neighbour and a switched-off host both look like 'no reply', and they have opposite fixes. Read from /proc, so no privileges are needed. One network namespace. (arguments: device)

analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)
lab_network_status: What a lab network can actually reach: a real ping from inside each subnet, not just what the routing table says. (arguments: name)

device_probe: What user-space driver routes this machine has: I2C buses, video devices, and FUSE mounts. Read-only, and reports unknown-with-a-reason where a list could not be read rather than claiming there is nothing.

file_locks: Show who holds a file lock, and on what - the answer to "why won't this file save" and "why did my write fail with EAGAIN". A WRITE lock blocks another writer; a READ lock is shared and usually harmless. Use for 'who has this file locked', 'what is holding a lock', 'why can't I write this file', 'is this file locked'. Give a path to check one file; omit it for every lock on the machine. Reads the kernel's own lock table (/proc/locks), so it needs no binary and no privilege. Read-only; nothing is polled, changed or broken. (arguments: path)

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

train.say: Read, create or edit Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.
train.positives_desc: office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

negatives.desc: calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

create_archive: Create a zip or tar.gz archive from files or folders, or list or safely extract an existing one. Refuses archives whose entries would escape the destination. (arguments: action, source, destination, format)

edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. The text to replace must appear exactly once, or nothing is written - the count and line numbers are reported instead of a guess being made. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

search_my_files: Search your own files by meaning - documents, notes, code - in a directory you choose, or your home if you name none. 'search': what matches a few words. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh the index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, path, limit)
create_directory: Create a directory, and any missing parent directories. Succeeds without complaint if it already exists. (arguments: path)
create_document: Create a document from a title and body: a markdown file, a plain text file, or an HTML page. Writes a new file; never overwrites. (arguments: title, body, format, path)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

train.say: Drive health and disk encryption.
train.positives_desc: disk_health: Health of this machine's drives (SMART/NVMe status and wear where it can be read) and whether each mounted filesystem - /, /home and the rest - sits on an encrypted (LUKS) volume. Use for 'is my SSD healthy', 'is my disk encrypted', 'how worn is my drive'. Drive health uses the 'storage-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

negatives.desc: ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

vm: Run a virtual machine with QEMU and drive it like a browser: launch it with a visible window on the desktop and a QMP control socket beside it, photograph its screen, send key combinations, type text into it, move and click its pointer (percentages of its screen), check its power state, and stop it. Requires the 'vm-control-enabled' consent key, off by default. Listing the VMs already running is `list_vms` (virsh) or this skill's list action; this one starts and drives them. (arguments: action, name, memory_mb, iso, disk, display, firmware, tpm, keys, text, x, y, button)

close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

arrange_window: Minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send a window to another workspace, by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. move takes x and y, resize takes width and height (pixels), set_workspace takes a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace)

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

train.say: How much battery do I have left?
train.positives_desc: get_battery_status: Get the current battery charge percentage and charging state.

negatives.desc: set_power_profile: Switch the machine between its power profiles - typically power-saver, balanced and performance - and report which one is active now. The profile list is read from the machine rather than assumed, because which profiles exist depends on the CPU driver: switching to one the machine does not have is refused with the valid names listed. Changes the CPU and platform power behaviour, not a per-application setting. (arguments: profile)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

power_action: Suspend (sleep), hibernate, restart or shut down this computer, or cancel a scheduled restart/shutdown. Restart and shutdown happen after one minute and can be cancelled. Requires the 'power-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)
click_pointer: Click a mouse button at the current pointer position. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: button, count)

charger_info: Report what is powering this machine: on battery or plugged in, AC adapter or USB-C, whether USB Power Delivery is in use, and the charger's wattage when the firmware reports it, plus battery charge and rate.

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

vm: Run a virtual machine with QEMU and drive it like a browser: launch it with a visible window on the desktop and a QMP control socket beside it, photograph its screen, send key combinations, type text into it, move and click its pointer (percentages of its screen), check its power state, and stop it. Requires the 'vm-control-enabled' consent key, off by default. Listing the VMs already running is `list_vms` (virsh) or this skill's list action; this one starts and drives them. (arguments: action, name, memory_mb, iso, disk, display, firmware, tpm, keys, text, x, y, button)

train.say: Call through a paired phone, on this computer's speakers.
train.positives_desc: bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

negatives.desc: phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': what the pairing half of the protocol is and why it is not here. Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

train.say: File size, age and permissions.
train.positives_desc: get_file_info: Report one file's type, size, when it was last modified, and who can read it. Use this to answer 'when did I last edit this' or 'who else can read this file' - no other skill reports timestamps or permissions. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: download_file: Download a file from a web address and save it to disk, reporting the size and how long it took. Use for 'download that file', 'get this installer', 'save that page'. Only http and https; a site that answers with an error page reports that rather than saving the error as if it were the file. (arguments: url, destination)

permission_audit: Find files and directories under a path that other users on this machine can read or write. Use for 'can anyone see my files', 'is anything private exposed', 'what is world-writable in here'. Leads with the proportion that is readable, because a raw count is noise on a working tree, and separates world-writable (replaceable by others) from world-readable. Flags files whose NAMES suggest secrets and says it is matching names, not contents. Changes nothing. (arguments: path)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

stale_files: Find files that are both large and untouched for a long time - the deletion candidates a disk-usage answer only gestures at. Use for 'what can I delete', 'what is safe to clean up', 'what in here is old and big'. Reports candidates only: it claims nothing is safe to delete, removes nothing, and says that an untouched timestamp is not proof a file is unused. Read-only. (arguments: path, older_than_days, limit)

delete_file: Delete a file or folder by moving it to the desktop trash, where it stays recoverable. This is how you clear something out. The whole folder goes as one item and can be restored from the trash - nothing in this project is deleted permanently, so there is no faster or 'real' delete to reach for instead. Requires the 'file-delete-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path)

edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. The text to replace must appear exactly once, or nothing is written - the count and line numbers are reported instead of a guess being made. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

file_locks: Show who holds a file lock, and on what - the answer to "why won't this file save" and "why did my write fail with EAGAIN". A WRITE lock blocks another writer; a READ lock is shared and usually harmless. Use for 'who has this file locked', 'what is holding a lock', 'why can't I write this file', 'is this file locked'. Give a path to check one file; omit it for every lock on the machine. Reads the kernel's own lock table (/proc/locks), so it needs no binary and no privilege. Read-only; nothing is polled, changed or broken. (arguments: path)

train.say: Compare two files.
train.positives_desc: compare_files: Show what is different between two text files, as a unified diff. Reports 'identical' when they match. Use this to compare two versions of a config, or to see what a change actually did. (arguments: path_a, path_b, context_lines)

negatives.desc: solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

cloud_files: See what is in this machine's configured cloud storage remotes - which remotes rclone knows, how many objects and bytes each holds, and what is at the top level of one. Use for 'what is in my cloud drive', 'is anything in the bucket', 'how big is my remote'. Read-only: it never copies, syncs or deletes anything. A machine with no remotes says so, because that means there is nowhere off-machine for anything to go. (arguments: remote, path)

duplicate_files: Find files with identical content under a directory, and how much space the copies waste. Use for 'why is my disk full', 'are there duplicates in my Downloads', 'where is my space going'. Reports verified groups only - same size is evidence, a matching hash is proof - and never marks one copy as the original. Read-only: it hashes and lists, and deletes nothing. (arguments: path, limit)

files_by_name: Find every file with a given name under a directory, with sizes and modification dates, so you can see whether they are copies. Use for 'where are all my report.docx', 'how many copies of this do I have', 'which is the newest'. Reports the newest and whether the sizes agree, and does NOT claim the contents match - duplicate_files answers that. Deletes nothing. (arguments: name, path, case_sensitive)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results)

log_files: See which log files under /var/log are largest, whether they are still being written to right now, and whether anything rotates them. Use for 'why is my disk full', 'what is filling up the disk', 'is that log growing'. Also reports logrotate configuration errors, which silently stop a rotation. Read-only: it runs logrotate in debug mode, which rotates nothing. (arguments: limit)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

train.say: Type text.
train.positives_desc: type_text: Type text at the currently focused window. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: text)

negatives.desc: space_by_type: Break disk usage down by kind of file - video, audio, image, document, archive, code and so on - across all directories, rather than per directory. Use for 'what is eating my disk', 'is it the photos or the documents', 'what takes up the space in here'. Names the largest category, and reports files whose type it could not tell as a visible `other` bucket rather than dropping them. Read-only. (arguments: path)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)
encode_text: Encode or decode text: base64, url (percent-encoding), hex, binary, rot13, morse. (arguments: text, scheme, direction)
read_text_file: Read a text file and return its contents, optionally a range of lines. Use this to see what a file actually says. (arguments: path, start_line, max_lines)

translate_text: Translate text into another language, using a local translation tool when one is installed and a web service otherwise. The reply says which was used, because one sends your text to a third party. (arguments: text, to_language, from_language)

write_text_file: Write text to a file, creating it or replacing its contents. Refuses to replace a non-empty file unless asked to overwrite, and refuses binary data. (arguments: path, content, overwrite, append)

train.say: Which interfaces are bridges, and what is plugged into them.
train.positives_desc: bridge_topology: Show which network interfaces are bridges, exactly which interfaces are enslaved to each one, and which are standalone. Answers 'is this interface actually plugged into the bridge it should be', which is the usual reason a network that reported no errors carries no traffic. Read from /sys so it needs no privileges and cannot be half-applied. Reports the plumbing, not whether traffic flows. Covers this network namespace only. (arguments: bridge)

negatives.desc: usb_devices: What is plugged into this machine's USB ports (mice, phones, webcams, sticks, with their speed), and every Thunderbolt/USB4 device with whether it is authorised to work. Use for 'what's plugged in', 'why doesn't my dock work', 'is my webcam connected'. The USB list uses the 'usb-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

pdf_pages: Work with PDF pages without re-rendering them: 'info' (page count), 'merge' several PDFs into one (paths, in order), 'split' a PDF into one file per page (into a folder), or 'extract' some pages (e.g. '1-3,7') into a new PDF. Always writes new files; never overwrites an existing one or changes the originals. No rotation. (arguments: action, path, paths, pages, output)

vm: Run a virtual machine with QEMU and drive it like a browser: launch it with a visible window on the desktop and a QMP control socket beside it, photograph its screen, send key combinations, type text into it, move and click its pointer (percentages of its screen), check its power state, and stop it. Requires the 'vm-control-enabled' consent key, off by default. Listing the VMs already running is `list_vms` (virsh) or this skill's list action; this one starts and drives them. (arguments: action, name, memory_mb, iso, disk, display, firmware, tpm, keys, text, x, y, button)

interface_counters: Report how many bytes and packets each network interface has carried, in each direction, with its error and drop counters, plus the machine's TCP retransmit and error totals. Totals are since each interface came up, and the figures are read from /proc so no daemon needs to be running. Optionally sample twice to get a rate. Read-only. Counts one network namespace: an interface inside a network namespace is not visible here. (arguments: interface, sample_seconds, limit)

charger_info: Report what is powering this machine: on battery or plugged in, AC adapter or USB-C, whether USB Power Delivery is in use, and the charger's wattage when the firmware reports it, plus battery charge and rate.

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

train.say: Save a multi-step goal to run later.
train.positives_desc: manage_goals: Save a multi-step goal as a plan of tool steps that can be run later from the Goals panel, list saved goals, answer one that is waiting for you, or remove one. Saving runs nothing. Each step names a tool, its arguments, and a name for its result; a later step can use an earlier result as $name in a string argument, and lists the names it depends_on. A depends_on name that no earlier step produces is a question for the user: the goal waits there until they answer it. Requires the 'goals-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, goal, steps, id, answer)

negatives.desc: routines: Save a routine: a short phrase (e.g. 'good morning', 'leaving work') that later runs a whole request, e.g. 'tell me the weather, my calendar today and the top news'. Also list or delete routines. Saving runs nothing; saying the phrase later runs the request. (arguments: action, name, request, phrases)

todo_list: Keep a list of tasks that survives between turns and restarts: add an item, change its status, mark what it is blocked by, or list what is outstanding. Use this to track a multi-step job rather than holding it in the conversation. Requires the 'todo-list-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, id, content, status, blocked_by)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)
kill_process: Stop a running process by pid, asking it to exit cleanly. Use list_processes to find the pid first. Requires the 'process-kill-enabled' consent key. (arguments: pid, signal_name)
check_internet: Check whether the internet is working and, if not, which step fails: network connection, router, internet, DNS, or websites. Also reports the delay to the router and to the internet.

undo_last_change: Put a file back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content recorded just before Chronoa's own last edit to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, steps)

train.say: what's on my clipboard?
train.positives_desc: get_clipboard: Read the current contents of the system clipboard.

negatives.desc: set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

train.say: set the volume to 40 percent
train.positives_desc: set_volume: Set the system output volume to an exact percentage. (arguments: percent, device)

negatives.desc: calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

set_brightness: Get or set screen brightness as a percentage. With no level, reports the current brightness of each panel. With a level, sets it. Writing needs root - the backlight node is root-owned - and a permission failure is reported as such rather than as success. (arguments: level)
set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

train.say: Download a model.
train.positives_desc: install_model: Download a named model into the local Ollama. Takes an explicit model name and never picks one by itself - call recommend_model first and install only what the user agreed to. Warns rather than refuses when the model looks larger than available memory. This downloads gigabytes and needs the network. (arguments: name)

negatives.desc: recommend_model: Recommend local language models that fit this machine's currently available memory, largest first, marking which support reliable tool calling. Reports available (not total) memory and the budget used. Does not download anything. (arguments: limit)

download_file: Download a file from a web address and save it to disk, reporting the size and how long it took. Use for 'download that file', 'get this installer', 'save that page'. Only http and https; a site that answers with an error page reports that rather than saving the error as if it were the file. (arguments: url, destination)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

notes: Keep your own notes in a plain list stored on this machine: 'add' one from 'text', 'list' them, 'search' by text or id, 'remove' one by 'id'. Never sent to a model. For what the assistant itself believes and uses in its replies, use remember_fact instead. (arguments: action, text, query, id)

system_info: Describe the machine Chronoa is running on: distribution, kernel, architecture, uptime, load, memory, CPU count, whether this is a desktop session or a container, and the hardware identity (make, model, board, BIOS version).

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

compute_hash: Compute a checksum of a file, and optionally compare it with an expected value. Defaults to SHA-256, which is what package managers and download sites publish. (arguments: path, algorithm, expected)

train.say: Click.
train.positives_desc: click_pointer: Click a mouse button at the current pointer position. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: button, count)

negatives.desc: close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

arrange_window: Minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send a window to another workspace, by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. move takes x and y, resize takes width and height (pixels), set_workspace takes a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace)

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

train.say: Commit notes.txt with the message 'update the notes'.
train.positives_desc: git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)

negatives.desc: notes: Keep your own notes in a plain list stored on this machine: 'add' one from 'text', 'list' them, 'search' by text or id, 'remove' one by 'id'. Never sent to a model. For what the assistant itself believes and uses in its replies, use remember_fact instead. (arguments: action, text, query, id)
convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)
create_document: Create a document from a title and body: a markdown file, a plain text file, or an HTML page. Writes a new file; never overwrites. (arguments: title, body, format, path)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

file_locks: Show who holds a file lock, and on what - the answer to "why won't this file save" and "why did my write fail with EAGAIN". A WRITE lock blocks another writer; a READ lock is shared and usually harmless. Use for 'who has this file locked', 'what is holding a lock', 'why can't I write this file', 'is this file locked'. Give a path to check one file; omit it for every lock on the machine. Reads the kernel's own lock table (/proc/locks), so it needs no binary and no privilege. Read-only; nothing is polled, changed or broken. (arguments: path)

meeting: Hold a meeting: record the microphone for as long as it takes, transcribe it with who said what, and write notes. 'record': start now and run for the given number of minutes (default 120, the ceiling). 'notes': write notes from a recording that already exists. 'status': what a meeting would do on this machine. The recording, the transcript and the notes are all written on this computer and nothing leaves it. Needs the 'meeting-enabled' consent key, which is off by default - this holds the microphone for possibly hours, with other people speaking. (arguments: action, minutes, path)

dns_lookup: Look a hostname or address up in DNS and report what came back: the addresses, or the mail servers, name servers, TXT records, certificate records or other records a name publishes, and whether the answer is DNSSEC-signed and valid. Distinguishes 'this name does not exist' from 'the resolver did not answer', because those have different fixes. Obeys privacy mode, since the query goes to a resolver outside this machine. Read-only. (arguments: name, type)

train.say: What is conflicting in a git repository, and resolve it.
train.positives_desc: resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

negatives.desc: git_inspect: Report a git working tree: what has changed and is not committed, the diff of those changes, recent commits, or the current branch and how far it is from its upstream; also the stashed work and the reflog (the record that survives rebases and amends). Reports UNKNOWN - never 'clean tree' - when git is missing, the folder is not a repository, or git fails. Requires the 'git-sense-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, subcommand, revision, since, context_lines)

git_push: Push a branch to a named remote. Requires the 'git-push-enabled' consent key, and asks before every push. The remote must be one the repository already has, and must be named - there is no default and no 'push everything'. Force-pushing is refused. (arguments: remote, branch, set_upstream, path)

git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)
git_branch: Create a branch in a git repository and switch to it, or switch to a branch that already exists. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. (arguments: name, path)

vcs_status: What state a checkout is in, for git, subversion or mercurial: which version control system it belongs to, the branch or revision, the repository it points at, and what has changed. Use when the answer might not be git - 'what is this folder's state', 'which repository is this', 'what changed in my checkout'. Read-only; runs nothing that modifies a repository. (arguments: path)

check_port: Check whether a specific port on a specific host accepts connections from this machine, and say why it does not - refused (the host is up, nothing is listening), timed out (a firewall, or a host that is off), or the name does not resolve. Use for 'is my server reachable', 'why can nothing connect to it', 'is port 443 open on that box'. Opens exactly one connection and sends nothing; it is not a scan. (arguments: host, port)

list_fonts: List the font families installed on this machine (optionally only those whose name contains some text), and which real font the generic names - sans-serif, serif, monospace, emoji - or a font you name actually resolve to. Use for 'what fonts do I have', 'is Fira Code installed', 'which font is used for monospace'. Read-only. (arguments: query)

train.say: What does Super+Tab do on this machine?
train.positives_desc: list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

negatives.desc: browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.

press_key: Press a key or key combination in the focused window, e.g. 'Return', 'Escape', 'Tab' or 'ctrl+shift+t'. This sends a key, not text - use type_text to type a string. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key. X11 only. (arguments: key, repeat)

apply_patch: Apply a .patch or .diff file to files on this machine. Use for 'apply this diff', 'here is a patch', 'merge this change in'. Runs a dry run by default and changes nothing until asked. Reports when the patch is already applied, which is a refusal rather than a reverse-applied change, and lists the .rej files patch leaves for hunks it could not apply. Never prompts. (arguments: patch, path, strip, action)

autostart_entries: Report everything on this machine that starts automatically: the autostart .desktop files in this user's home and /etc/xdg, the enabled systemd user units and timers, and the crontab. Use for 'what starts automatically', 'what runs at login', 'what is scheduled', 'why does this thing keep running', 'what did I set to start on its own'. Honours Hidden, OnlyShowIn and NotShowIn, and says 'cannot tell' rather than guessing when the desktop is unknown - which is the normal state outside a login session. Read-only; nothing is enabled, disabled or changed.

backup_status: Whether this machine's files are actually backed up off it: how many restic snapshots exist, when the most recent was taken, what it covered, and whether the repository still passes restic's own integrity check. Use for 'is my backup working', 'when did I last back up', 'do I have a copy of my files'. A machine with no repository configured says so plainly, because that means there is no backup. Read-only: it never writes to the repository. (arguments: repository)

bandwidth_to_host: Measure how fast this machine can send data to another machine over the network, using a controlled iperf3 transfer. Use for 'why is my NAS slow', 'how fast is my network to the server', 'is the bottleneck the network or the disk'. Needs iperf3 running on the other machine - ask for loopback to measure this machine against itself. Read-only: it transfers data and writes nothing. (arguments: host, port, seconds)

train.say: find me a rocket emoji
train.positives_desc: find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)

negatives.desc: find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'.
