This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

list_fonts: List the font families installed on this machine (optionally only those whose name contains some text), and which real font the generic names - sans-serif, serif, monospace, emoji - or a font you name actually resolve to. Use for 'what fonts do I have', 'is Fira Code installed', 'which font is used for monospace'. Read-only. (arguments: query)

list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

train.say: Copy this to the clipboard
train.positives_desc: set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

negatives.desc: get_clipboard: Read the current contents of the system clipboard.

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

backup_status: Whether this machine's files are actually backed up off it: how many restic snapshots exist, when the most recent was taken, what it covered, and whether the repository still passes restic's own integrity check. Use for 'is my backup working', 'when did I last back up', 'do I have a copy of my files'. A machine with no repository configured says so plainly, because that means there is no backup. Read-only: it never writes to the repository. (arguments: repository)

train.say: Set a timer for 5 minutes.
train.positives_desc: set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

negatives.desc: scheduled_tasks: What is scheduled to run on this machine: your crontab, the system crontab and /etc/cron.d, and both the system and your systemd timers. Each source is reported separately and one that cannot be read says so, because a machine can have no user crontab and still have nine timers. Reading what the machine has scheduled describes the machine rather than the person's world, so it needs no permission. Nothing is scheduled, changed or removed by asking. (arguments: source)

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

set_sleep_inhibit: Report what is currently holding the machine awake, or take a bounded hold so it does not sleep for a while, or release ours. Use for 'keep it awake while I...' - a long install, a backup, a test run. Scoped and self-lapsing; to change the machine's idle timeout permanently use set_screensaver instead. Gated by 'sleep-inhibit-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, reason, seconds)

autostart_entries: Report everything on this machine that starts automatically: the autostart .desktop files in this user's home and /etc/xdg, the enabled systemd user units and timers, and the crontab. Use for 'what starts automatically', 'what runs at login', 'what is scheduled', 'why does this thing keep running', 'what did I set to start on its own'. Honours Hidden, OnlyShowIn and NotShowIn, and says 'cannot tell' rather than guessing when the desktop is unknown - which is the normal state outside a login session. Read-only; nothing is enabled, disabled or changed.

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

print_queue: Show the printers, which one is the default, the print jobs still waiting, and what this machine can print to even when nothing is configured; or cancel a waiting job by its id. Use for 'what's printing', 'why isn't my printer there', 'what can I print to', 'cancel that print'. Cancelling requires the 'print-control-enabled' consent key; listing does not. (arguments: action, job, printer, option)

set_brightness: Get or set screen brightness as a percentage. With no level, reports the current brightness of each panel. With a level, sets it. Writing needs root - the backlight node is root-owned - and a permission failure is reported as such rather than as success. (arguments: level)

train.say: Installed fonts, and which one is used.
train.positives_desc: list_fonts: List the font families installed on this machine (optionally only those whose name contains some text), and which real font the generic names - sans-serif, serif, monospace, emoji - or a font you name actually resolve to. Use for 'what fonts do I have', 'is Fira Code installed', 'which font is used for monospace'. Read-only. (arguments: query)

negatives.desc: install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

install_model: Download a named model into the local Ollama. Takes an explicit model name and never picks one by itself - call recommend_model first and install only what the user agreed to. Warns rather than refuses when the model looks larger than available memory. This downloads gigabytes and needs the network. (arguments: name)

set_sleep_inhibit: Report what is currently holding the machine awake, or take a bounded hold so it does not sleep for a while, or release ours. Use for 'keep it awake while I...' - a long install, a backup, a test run. Scoped and self-lapsing; to change the machine's idle timeout permanently use set_screensaver instead. Gated by 'sleep-inhibit-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, reason, seconds)

translate_text: Translate text into another language, using a local translation tool when one is installed and a web service otherwise. The reply says which was used, because one sends your text to a third party. (arguments: text, to_language, from_language)

read_document: Read the text of a PDF (optionally a page range) or of an image (OCR), e.g. to summarise it or read it out. For a PDF it also reports whether the document embeds its fonts, since one that does not prints wrong elsewhere. (arguments: path, first_page, last_page)

sing: Sing a line aloud: each syllable gets its own note, on one of five named contours (rising, falling, arch, level, wave) or the real tune from a 'midi_file'. It does NOT know any song, so never present its output as a particular tune unless a MIDI file was supplied. Needs soundtouch or rubberband. (arguments: text, shape, voice_style, midi_file)

vm: Run a virtual machine with QEMU and drive it like a browser: launch it with a visible window on the desktop and a QMP control socket beside it, photograph its screen, send key combinations, type text into it, move and click its pointer (percentages of its screen), check its power state, and stop it. Requires the 'vm-control-enabled' consent key, off by default. Listing the VMs already running is `list_vms` (virsh) or this skill's list action; this one starts and drives them. (arguments: action, name, memory_mb, iso, disk, display, firmware, tpm, keys, text, x, y, button)

train.say: Change the keyboard layout.
train.positives_desc: set_keyboard_layout: List the keyboard layouts this system knows, report the one in use, or switch to another. Changing it requires the existing 'input-control-enabled' consent key; listing needs no permission. (arguments: action, layout)

negatives.desc: disk_layout: Show how this machine's disks are partitioned: every physical disk, each partition with its size, filesystem and purpose (EFI, Linux root, /home, LUKS, LVM, swap), and where each one is mounted. Use for 'how is my disk partitioned', 'what partitions are on this machine', 'which partition is my home directory on', 'is my disk GPT or plain', 'what is this LUKS partition for'. Follows the storage sense's consent switch, because it reports the same machine. Read-only; nothing is changed. Loop devices (the immutable snap images) are hidden unless show_hidden is set, and their count is always stated. (arguments: show_hidden)

undo_last_change: Put a file back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content recorded just before Chronoa's own last edit to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, steps)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

train.say: Find, ping or send a file to your paired phone.
train.positives_desc: phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

negatives.desc: lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': what the pairing half of the protocol is and why it is not here. Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

ping_host: Ping a named host or IP address and report whether it answers, how long the replies take and how many were lost. Use this when a specific host is slow or unreachable; 'check_internet' only answers whether the internet works at all. (arguments: host, count)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. The text to replace must appear exactly once, or nothing is written - the count and line numbers are reported instead of a guess being made. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

train.say: Save a phrase that runs a whole request.
train.positives_desc: routines: Save a routine: a short phrase (e.g. 'good morning', 'leaving work') that later runs a whole request, e.g. 'tell me the weather, my calendar today and the top news'. Also list or delete routines. Saving runs nothing; saying the phrase later runs the request. (arguments: action, name, request, phrases)

negatives.desc: git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)

calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)
kill_process: Stop a running process by pid, asking it to exit cleanly. Use list_processes to find the pid first. Requires the 'process-kill-enabled' consent key. (arguments: pid, signal_name)

manage_goals: Save a multi-step goal as a plan of tool steps that can be run later from the Goals panel, list saved goals, answer one that is waiting for you, or remove one. Saving runs nothing. Each step names a tool, its arguments, and a name for its result; a later step can use an earlier result as $name in a string argument, and lists the names it depends_on. A depends_on name that no earlier step produces is a question for the user: the goal waits there until they answer it. Requires the 'goals-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, goal, steps, id, answer)

ask_user: Ask the user a clarifying question and wait for their answer, with 2 to 4 short options they can pick. Use this whenever a request is genuinely ambiguous - especially when several files or devices could match. Do not guess instead, and do not ask when one option is obviously right. In a headless session there is nobody to answer and this will say so. (arguments: question, options)

list_apps: List the applications installed on this machine, optionally filtered by a search term, so a request to open something can be answered with what actually exists rather than a guess. (arguments: search)

train.say: Turn on the screen reader
train.positives_desc: accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

negatives.desc: container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

lock_screen: Lock this session so a password is needed to come back to it. Uses the session's own mechanism so the same thing happens as the desktop's Lock button. Requires the 'screen-lock-enabled' consent key.

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

fingerprint_status: Whether fingerprint login is set up on this machine, and which fingers are enrolled. Says which of the four real states it is in: no reader attached, reader present but nothing enrolled, fingers enrolled, or the daemon not running and the question unanswerable. Reading only - it never enrolls or deletes a fingerprint, because 'which fingers are enrolled' is a question and the other two are not. Needs no permission: it reports a machine's own login configuration, and the answer is about hardware and a per-user setting rather than anything private. (arguments: user)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

train.say: Find and replace.
train.positives_desc: find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

negatives.desc: office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. The text to replace must appear exactly once, or nothing is written - the count and line numbers are reported instead of a guess being made. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

train.say: turn on do not disturb
train.positives_desc: do_not_disturb: Turn Do Not Disturb on (silence notification pop-ups) or off, or say whether it is on. (arguments: enabled)

negatives.desc: watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)
notify: Send a desktop notification to the user. Honours the 'notification-enabled' setting, so it refuses quietly when notifications are turned off. (arguments: summary, body)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

train.say: Read a picture's dimensions, format, and colour.
train.positives_desc: read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: screenshot: Capture the screen to a PNG file and return the path it was saved to. Refuses when there is no display.

solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

qr_code: read: decode every QR code and barcode in a picture (path) or on the screen (screen=true, needs the vision consent). create: make a QR code PNG of text (a URL, Wi-Fi details, a note) at output. (arguments: action, path, screen, text, output)

train.say: Change when the screen blanks and locks.
train.positives_desc: set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

negatives.desc: lock_screen: Lock this session so a password is needed to come back to it. Uses the session's own mechanism so the same thing happens as the desktop's Lock button. Requires the 'screen-lock-enabled' consent key.

set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

file_locks: Show who holds a file lock, and on what - the answer to "why won't this file save" and "why did my write fail with EAGAIN". A WRITE lock blocks another writer; a READ lock is shared and usually harmless. Use for 'who has this file locked', 'what is holding a lock', 'why can't I write this file', 'is this file locked'. Give a path to check one file; omit it for every lock on the machine. Reads the kernel's own lock table (/proc/locks), so it needs no binary and no privilege. Read-only; nothing is polled, changed or broken. (arguments: path)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

undo_last_change: Put a file back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content recorded just before Chronoa's own last edit to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, steps)

set_wallpaper: Report or change the GNOME desktop wallpaper, setting the light and dark variants together. Refuses a path that does not exist, rather than leaving a blank desktop with no error. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, image)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

train.say: mute the sound
train.positives_desc: set_mute: Mute or unmute the sound from the speakers or headphones ('mute the sound', 'unmute'). The microphone is set_mic_mute. (arguments: mute, device)

negatives.desc: set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)
set_volume: Set the system output volume to an exact percentage. (arguments: percent, device)

set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

train.say: who said what in ~/Music/meeting.m4a?
train.positives_desc: recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

negatives.desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

meeting: Hold a meeting: record the microphone for as long as it takes, transcribe it with who said what, and write notes. 'record': start now and run for the given number of minutes (default 120, the ceiling). 'notes': write notes from a recording that already exists. 'status': what a meeting would do on this machine. The recording, the transcript and the notes are all written on this computer and nothing leaves it. Needs the 'meeting-enabled' consent key, which is off by default - this holds the microphone for possibly hours, with other people speaking. (arguments: action, minutes, path)

edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

train.say: Find your photos by what is in them, what is written on them, or when they were taken.
train.positives_desc: photos: Find the user's photos by what is in them or written on them, or when they were taken. search: query like 'receipt hardware shop', 'dog on the beach', 'december 2025'; index: update the index of the Pictures folder (a batch at a time); status: how much is indexed. (arguments: action, query, captions)

negatives.desc: photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

log_files: See which log files under /var/log are largest, whether they are still being written to right now, and whether anything rotates them. Use for 'why is my disk full', 'what is filling up the disk', 'is that log growing'. Also reports logrotate configuration errors, which silently stop a rotation. Read-only: it runs logrotate in debug mode, which rotates nothing. (arguments: limit)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

train.say: give ~/Pictures/beach.jpg a sepia look

For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

photos: Find the user's photos by what is in them or written on them, or when they were taken. search: query like 'receipt hardware shop', 'dog on the beach', 'december 2025'; index: update the index of the Pictures folder (a batch at a time); status: how much is indexed. (arguments: action, query, captions)
