train.positives_desc: speak: Speak text aloud using the local text-to-speech engine. Reuses the app's own Piper/RHVoice/espeak-ng fallback chain and its own audio playback path. The engine actually used is named in the result. (arguments: text)

negatives.desc: browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

backup_status: Whether this machine's files are actually backed up off it: how many restic snapshots exist, when the most recent was taken, what it covered, and whether the repository still passes restic's own integrity check. Use for 'is my backup working', 'when did I last back up', 'do I have a copy of my files'. A machine with no repository configured says so plainly, because that means there is no backup. Read-only: it never writes to the repository. (arguments: repository)

control_service: Start, stop, restart, reload, enable or disable a system service, then read its state back so the reply says whether it actually came up. Requires the 'service-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: unit, action)

dns_lookup: Look a hostname or address up in DNS and report what came back: the addresses, or the mail servers, name servers, TXT records, certificate records or other records a name publishes, and whether the answer is DNSSEC-signed and valid. Distinguishes 'this name does not exist' from 'the resolver did not answer', because those have different fixes. Obeys privacy mode, since the query goes to a resolver outside this machine. Read-only. (arguments: name, type)

driver_build: Build a scaffolded out-of-tree kernel module with Kbuild, then read the resulting .ko back off disk. Needs the 'driver-build-enabled' consent key. Refuses with the missing package named when this machine has no toolchain. (arguments: name, path)

graphics_stack: Report whether OpenGL is hardware accelerated or falling back to software (llvmpipe). Answers from sysfs for the kernel driver - always, with no display needed - and from glxinfo -B for the renderer string, which is the only thing that actually says hardware or software. Use for 'is my graphics accelerated', 'why is this game slow', 'is my GPU being used', 'what graphics card renderer am I on'. Says which of the two it could not read and why, and never reports a crashed tool as a fact about the GPU. Read-only; nothing is changed.

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

snapshot_status: Whether this Shanios machine can roll back: the OS version, which blue/green slot was booted, which slot boots next, the previous slot a rollback would return to, any recorded boot failure or pending reboot, and the btrfs snapshots on disk. Use for 'can I undo the update', 'which slot am I on', 'is an update waiting'. The snapshot list uses the 'snapshots-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

train.say: Switch speakers, headphones and microphones.
train.positives_desc: audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

negatives.desc: bluetooth_devices: List paired Bluetooth devices (and which are connected), or connect / disconnect one by its name, e.g. 'connect my headphones'. (arguments: action, name)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

usb_devices: What is plugged into this machine's USB ports (mice, phones, webcams, sticks, with their speed), and every Thunderbolt/USB4 device with whether it is authorised to work. Use for 'what's plugged in', 'why doesn't my dock work', 'is my webcam connected'. The USB list uses the 'usb-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

toggle_bluetooth: Turn the Bluetooth adapter on or off, or report its state and the paired devices. Requires the 'bluetooth-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

connect_wifi: Join a WiFi network by name, or leave the current one. Open networks only - this never handles a password, because a password passed through a chat or an MCP client is in a transcript. Requires the 'wifi-connect-enabled' consent key. (arguments: ssid)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

train.say: draw a lighthouse at sunset
train.positives_desc: generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. Saves a PNG and returns its path. (arguments: prompt, avoid, size, steps, seed, output, from_photo, strength)

negatives.desc: generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

get_weather: Current weather and today's forecast - temperature, feels-like, rain, wind - for a named place, or for where this computer is if no place is given; with `when`, the forecast for tomorrow, a weekday, this week or the weekend instead. Use for weather, temperature outside, rain, forecast. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: place, when)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

routines: Save a routine: a short phrase (e.g. 'good morning', 'leaving work') that later runs a whole request, e.g. 'tell me the weather, my calendar today and the top news'. Also list or delete routines. Saving runs nothing; saying the phrase later runs the request. (arguments: action, name, request, phrases)

convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

train.say: Close a window.
train.positives_desc: close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

negatives.desc: browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

arrange_window: Minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send a window to another workspace, by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. move takes x and y, resize takes width and height (pixels), set_workspace takes a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace)

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

list_apps: List the applications installed on this machine, optionally filtered by a search term, so a request to open something can be answered with what actually exists rather than a guess. (arguments: search)

train.say: Data used.
train.positives_desc: data_usage: How much internet data this computer has used today and this month, per network interface (from vnStat).

negatives.desc: disk_usage: Report how full each filesystem is, and optionally which directories under a given path use the most space. Read-only: it never deletes anything. (arguments: path)

explain_command: Explain a Linux shell command (not a general topic) from the local manuals (tldr, man), e.g. 'what does tar do', 'how do I use rsync'; or find which command does something, e.g. 'which command shows disk usage'. (arguments: command, task)

space_by_type: Break disk usage down by kind of file - video, audio, image, document, archive, code and so on - across all directories, rather than per directory. Use for 'what is eating my disk', 'is it the photos or the documents', 'what takes up the space in here'. Names the largest category, and reports files whose type it could not tell as a visible `other` bucket rather than dropping them. Read-only. (arguments: path)

stale_files: Find files that are both large and untouched for a long time - the deletion candidates a disk-usage answer only gestures at. Use for 'what can I delete', 'what is safe to clean up', 'what in here is old and big'. Reports candidates only: it claims nothing is safe to delete, removes nothing, and says that an untouched timestamp is not proof a file is unused. Read-only. (arguments: path, older_than_days, limit)

analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)

bandwidth_to_host: Measure how fast this machine can send data to another machine over the network, using a controlled iperf3 transfer. Use for 'why is my NAS slow', 'how fast is my network to the server', 'is the bottleneck the network or the disk'. Needs iperf3 running on the other machine - ask for loopback to measure this machine against itself. Read-only: it transfers data and writes nothing. (arguments: host, port, seconds)

calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

train.say: take a screenshot
train.positives_desc: screenshot: Capture the screen to a PNG file and return the path it was saved to. Refuses when there is no display.

negatives.desc: take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

json_query: Ask questions about the shape of a JSON document: what keys it has, what a field contains, how many entries an array has, or the sum/unique/sorted values of an array. Give either a file path or paste the document itself. (arguments: path, document, field, operation, of)

ping_host: Ping a named host or IP address and report whether it answers, how long the replies take and how many were lost. Use this when a specific host is slow or unreachable; 'check_internet' only answers whether the internet works at all. (arguments: host, count)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

set_sleep_inhibit: Report what is currently holding the machine awake, or take a bounded hold so it does not sleep for a while, or release ours. Use for 'keep it awake while I...' - a long install, a backup, a test run. Scoped and self-lapsing; to change the machine's idle timeout permanently use set_screensaver instead. Gated by 'sleep-inhibit-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, reason, seconds)

train.say: Open a file.
train.positives_desc: open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

identify_file: Identify a file by reading its first bytes rather than trusting its name. Use for 'why won't this open', 'what is this file', 'is this really a PNG', 'this file has no extension'. Reports the detected format and whether the filename agrees with it, which is the usual cause of a file refusing to open in the program its name implies. Says plainly when a signature is unrecognised. Read-only. (arguments: path)

Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

(arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

train.say: Which addresses on this link have answered, and which never have.
train.positives_desc: neighbour_table: Show the neighbour (ARP) table for this machine: which addresses on this link have answered, which have never answered and are holding packets instead of sending them, and which have gone stale. That distinction is the one layer 3 cannot make - an unresolved neighbour and a switched-off host both look like 'no reply', and they have opposite fixes. Read from /proc, so no privileges are needed. One network namespace. (arguments: device)

negatives.desc: dns_lookup: Look a hostname or address up in DNS and report what came back: the addresses, or the mail servers, name servers, TXT records, certificate records or other records a name publishes, and whether the answer is DNSSEC-signed and valid. Distinguishes 'this name does not exist' from 'the resolver did not answer', because those have different fixes. Obeys privacy mode, since the query goes to a resolver outside this machine. Read-only. (arguments: name, type)

nfc: Read and write NFC tags. 'scan': is there a reader here (most laptops have none, and that is a true answer). 'read': tap a tag and be told what is written on it. 'write': put a link on an Ultralight/NTAG sticker - a bank card, transit pass or hotel key is refused, not rewritten. 'emulate': present a tag to a phone. Needs the 'nfc-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, url, text, seconds, target)

scan_network: Find which devices are on the local network, with their names, addresses and hardware vendors. Local addresses only. Requires the network sense to be enabled. (arguments: range, resolve_names)

discover_hosts: Find which devices are on this network right now, by asking rather than by reading the cache - so devices that have never talked to this machine are found too. Reports an address and a hardware address for each, and counts devices answering on more than one address. The range is always the private network this machine is on; pass network= for a different private range, and a public one is refused. Connects to nothing it finds and reads no packet contents. Needs raw-socket access, so unprivileged it may report that rather than a partial sweep. (arguments: interface, network)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

broken_symlinks: Find symbolic links that point at nothing under a directory. Use for 'this shortcut does not work', 'clean up my dead links', 'what is broken in here'. Separates four cases: resolving links, dangling ones, cycles, and links whose target lies OUTSIDE the searched tree - which are not broken, only unverified from here. Never removes anything. (arguments: path)

binary_hardening: Report whether a binary is hardened: PIE, RELRO, full RELRO (BIND_NOW), stack canary and no-execute stack, each with what it stops. Use for 'is /path/to/this safe to run', 'is this binary hardened', 'does this have a stack canary', 'is this ASLR enabled'. Works on executables and shared libraries alike, and says 'not applicable' where a property genuinely has no answer rather than reporting it as missing. Read-only; nothing is loaded or written. (arguments: path)

train.say: Look a name up in DNS, or read its mail, name or certificate records.

negatives.desc: tls_certificate: Read a website's TLS certificate: when it expires, who issued it, and which hostnames it covers. Use for 'when does this site's certificate expire' or 'why is HTTPS failing on this'. (arguments: host, port)

search_my_files: Search your own files by meaning - documents, notes, code - in a directory you choose, or your home if you name none. 'search': what matches a few words. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh the index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, path, limit)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

search_documents: Search inside the user's files by their contents, using the desktop's own search index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). Requires the 'document-search-enabled' consent key. (arguments: query, kind, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

files_by_name: Find every file with a given name under a directory, with sizes and modification dates, so you can see whether they are copies. Use for 'where are all my report.docx', 'how many copies of this do I have', 'which is the newest'. Reports the newest and whether the sizes agree, and does NOT claim the contents match - duplicate_files answers that. Deletes nothing. (arguments: name, path, case_sensitive)

train.say: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off.
train.positives_desc: toggle_wifi: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off (only Wi-Fi - airplane_mode switches every radio, connect_wifi joins a network), or report whether Wi-Fi is on. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key; status needs no permission. (arguments: action)

negatives.desc: airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': what the pairing half of the protocol is and why it is not here. Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

qr_code: read: decode every QR code and barcode in a picture (path) or on the screen (screen=true, needs the vision consent). create: make a QR code PNG of text (a URL, Wi-Fi details, a note) at output. (arguments: action, path, screen, text, output)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

negatives.desc: whois_lookup: Look up who a domain or IP address is registered to: the registrar, when it was created, when it expires, its status and its name servers. Obeys privacy mode, because the answer can name a person. Tells a registry's rate-limit refusal apart from 'this domain is not registered', which are very different facts. Read-only, though it necessarily contacts a registry outside this machine. (arguments: domain)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). (arguments: target, action, app)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

nfc: Read and write NFC tags. 'scan': is there a reader here (most laptops have none, and that is a true answer). 'read': tap a tag and be told what is written on it. 'write': put a link on an Ultralight/NTAG sticker - a bank card, transit pass or hotel key is refused, not rewritten. 'emulate': present a tag to a phone. Needs the 'nfc-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, url, text, seconds, target)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

cloud_files: See what is in this machine's configured cloud storage remotes - which remotes rclone knows, how many objects and bytes each holds, and what is at the top level of one. Use for 'what is in my cloud drive', 'is anything in the bucket', 'how big is my remote'. Read-only: it never copies, syncs or deletes anything. A machine with no remotes says so, because that means there is nowhere off-machine for anything to go. (arguments: remote, path)

install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

train.say: What time is it?
train.positives_desc: get_datetime: The current date and time here. For the time in another city or country, use get_world_time.

negatives.desc: get_world_time: The current time and date in ANOTHER city, country or time zone, e.g. 'what time is it in Tokyo'. For the time here, use get_datetime. (arguments: place)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). train.say: Ask what a JSON document contains.

negatives.desc: convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)

scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

search_documents: Search inside the user's files by their contents, using the desktop's own search index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). Requires the 'document-search-enabled' consent key. (arguments: query, kind, limit)

In a headless session there is nobody to answer and this will say so. (arguments: question, options)

train.say: System services.
train.positives_desc: list_services: List system services with their load and active state, optionally filtered by name, newest state first for anything running. Reports UNKNOWN on a machine that is not systemd-managed. (arguments: name_filter, failed_only)

negatives.desc: bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

system_history: What this machine's CPU, disk, memory or paging was doing earlier, from the sysstat accounting records rather than a live reading. Use for 'was this busy last night', 'what was using the disk at lunchtime', 'why was the fan loud earlier'. boot_report: How the last boot went: total boot time split into firmware, loader, kernel and userspace, the services that took longest to start, when the machine booted and whether it shut down cleanly before, and which EFI entry the firmware will boot by default. machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.
check_updates: Check whether this machine has package updates waiting, without installing anything and without needing root. Works on Arch and other pacman systems.

train.say: generate a strong password
train.positives_desc: generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

negatives.desc: generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. Saves a PNG and returns its path. (arguments: prompt, avoid, size, steps, seed, output, from_photo, strength)

lab_network_create: Build an isolated lab network on this machine: a network namespace holding a bridge, with named subnets in namespaces of their own. set_hostname: Report this computer's name (hostname), or rename it - the name other devices on the network and in Bluetooth see. The name must be letters, digits and hyphens only. Renaming requires the 'hostname-control-enabled' consent key and the administrator password; reporting needs neither. (arguments: action, name)

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. train.say: write 'buy milk' into a new file ~/shopping.txt
train.positives_desc: write_text_file: Write text to a file, creating it or replacing its contents. Refuses to replace a non-empty file unless asked to overwrite, and refuses binary data. (arguments: path, content, overwrite, append)

negatives.desc: convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

train.say: is my internet working?
train.positives_desc: check_internet: Check whether the internet is working and, if not, which step fails: network connection, router, internet, DNS, or websites. Also reports the delay to the router and to the internet.

For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. Names the largest category, and reports files whose type it could not tell as a visible `other` bucket rather than dropping them. Read-only. (arguments: path)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

train.say: convert 10 miles to kilometers
train.positives_desc: convert_units: Convert a quantity between units: km/miles, kg/pounds, °C/°F, litres/gallons, km/h/mph, acres/hectares, GB/GiB, hours/minutes and so on. (arguments: value, from_unit, to_unit)

negatives.desc: calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

check_units: Check whether systemd unit files are valid and say what is wrong with them - a missing ExecStart binary, an unknown key, a dependency that does not exist - by running systemd-analyze verify on just the units you name. With no unit named, lists the services this machine has. This is a static check of the file: it does not know whether a dependency is down or a path is mounted, so a clean report does not promise the service will start. Reading only; nothing is started, stopped or changed. (arguments: unit)
convert_color: Convert a colour between hex (#ff8800), rgb(255, 136, 0), hsl and its CSS name. (arguments: color)

convert_currency: Convert an amount of money between currencies (rupees, dollars, euros, pounds, yen, ...) at today's ECB reference rate. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: amount, from_currency, to_currency)
convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)

convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

train.say: Convert a document between md, txt, and html.
train.positives_desc: convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)

negatives.desc: create_document: Create a document from a title and body: a markdown file, a plain text file, or an HTML page. Writes a new file; never overwrites. (arguments: title, body, format, path)
convert_color: Convert a colour between hex (#ff8800), rgb(255, 136, 0), hsl and its CSS name. (arguments: color)

convert_currency: Convert an amount of money between currencies (rupees, dollars, euros, pounds, yen, ...) at today's ECB reference rate. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: amount, from_currency, to_currency)
convert_units: Convert a quantity between units: km/miles, kg/pounds, °C/°F, litres/gallons, km/h/mph, acres/hectares, GB/GiB, hours/minutes and so on. (arguments: value, from_unit, to_unit)

convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

read_document: Read the text of a PDF (optionally a page range) or of an image (OCR), e.g. to summarise it or read it out. For a PDF it also reports whether the document embeds its fonts, since one that does not prints wrong elsewhere. (arguments: path, first_page, last_page)

train.say: Move or copy.
train.positives_desc: move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)

negatives.desc: move_pointer: Move the pointer to absolute screen coordinates. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: x, y)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

arrange_window: Minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send a window to another workspace, by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. move takes x and y, resize takes width and height (pixels), set_workspace takes a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

train.say: Add, move or cancel a calendar event.
train.positives_desc: calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

negatives.desc: calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)
calendar_month: Show the calendar for a month (default this month), with today marked. (arguments: month, year)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)
move_pointer: Move the pointer to absolute screen coordinates. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: x, y)

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)

date_math: Date arithmetic: days until a date ('how many days until 25 December'), the date N days/weeks/months from a date ('what date is 45 days from now'), days between two dates, or the weekday of a date. (arguments: operation, date, other_date, amount, unit)

train.say: Arm an automatic rule.
train.positives_desc: manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Listing needs no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds)

(arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

driver_scaffold: Write a real out-of-tree Linux kernel module project into a directory under your home: the C source, the Kbuild Makefile, a dkms.conf, a udev rule and a README. Creates new files and never overwrites an existing one. (arguments: name, path)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

train.say: What can I clean up to free space?
train.positives_desc: cleanup_report: Report what could be cleaned up to free disk space - trash, caches, the system log, unused Flatpak runtimes - with sizes. Reads only; deletes nothing.

negatives.desc: cleanup_apply: Actually free the disk space cleanup_report measured: empty your cache folder, or remove Flatpak runtimes no app uses. Both are recoverable or provably unused. Requires the 'cleanup-enabled' consent key. The system log is not here - that needs root, which Chronoa cannot ask for from inside a tool call. (arguments: target)

space_by_type: Break disk usage down by kind of file - video, audio, image, document, archive, code and so on - across all directories, rather than per directory. Use for 'what is eating my disk', 'is it the photos or the documents', 'what takes up the space in here'. Names the largest category, and reports files whose type it could not tell as a visible `other` bucket rather than dropping them. Read-only. (arguments: path)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, language, people, seconds)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

compression_savings: How much space btrfs compression is saving on this machine: the uncompressed size of the data, how much disk it actually occupies, and which compressor is doing it. Use for 'how much is compression saving me', 'why is my disk less full than the files suggest'. Read-only; nothing is changed.
disk_usage: Report how full each filesystem is, and optionally which directories under a given path use the most space. Read-only: it never deletes anything. (arguments: path)

duplicate_files: Find files with identical content under a directory, and how much space the copies waste. Use for 'why is my disk full', 'are there duplicates in my Downloads', 'where is my space going'. Reports verified groups only - same size is evidence, a matching hash is proof - and never marks one copy as the original. Read-only: it hashes and lists, and deletes nothing. (arguments: path, limit)

train.say: Trim, resize, rotate, or mute a video.
train.positives_desc: edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

negatives.desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)
set_mute: Mute or unmute the sound from the speakers or headphones ('mute the sound', 'unmute'). The microphone is set_mic_mute. (arguments: mute, device)

train.say: Open windows.
train.positives_desc: list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

negatives.desc: arrange_window: Minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send a window to another workspace, by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. move takes x and y, resize takes width and height (pixels), set_workspace takes a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace)

close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

train.say: Ask a clarifying question.
train.positives_desc: ask_user: Ask the user a clarifying question and wait for their answer, with 2 to 4 short options they can pick. Use this whenever a request is genuinely ambiguous - especially when several files or devices could match. Do not guess instead, and do not ask when one option is obviously right. In a headless session there is nobody to answer and this will say so. (arguments: question, options)

negatives.desc: analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)

json_query: Ask questions about the shape of a JSON document: what keys it has, what a field contains, how many entries an array has, or the sum/unique/sorted values of an array. Give either a file path or paste the document itself. (arguments: path, document, field, operation, of)

fingerprint_status: Whether fingerprint login is set up on this machine, and which fingers are enrolled. Says which of the four real states it is in: no reader attached, reader present but nothing enrolled, fingers enrolled, or the daemon not running and the question unanswerable. Reading only - it never enrolls or deletes a fingerprint, because 'which fingers are enrolled' is a question and the other two are not. Needs no permission: it reports a machine's own login configuration, and the answer is about hardware and a per-user setting rather than anything private. (arguments: user)

list_processes: List the processes running on this machine, with their pid, name, owner, CPU and memory use, sorted by CPU unless sort_by says otherwise. Use this to find what is using the machine - pass sort_by='memory' for the RAM question, which CPU order does not answer - or the pid of something you want to stop. (arguments: name_filter, sort_by, limit)

manage_goals: Save a multi-step goal as a plan of tool steps that can be run later from the Goals panel, list saved goals, answer one that is waiting for you, or remove one. Saving runs nothing. Each step names a tool, its arguments, and a name for its result; a later step can use an earlier result as $name in a string argument, and lists the names it depends_on. A depends_on name that no earlier step produces is a question for the user: the goal waits there until they answer it. Requires the 'goals-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, goal, steps, id, answer)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

apply_patch: Apply a .patch or .diff file to files on this machine. Use for 'apply this diff', 'here is a patch', 'merge this change in'. Runs a dry run by default and changes nothing until asked. Reports when the patch is already applied, which is a refusal rather than a reverse-applied change, and lists the .rej files patch leaves for hunks it could not apply. Never prompts. (arguments: patch, path, strip, action)

train.say: Join a WiFi network.
train.positives_desc: connect_wifi: Join a WiFi network by name, or leave the current one. Open networks only - this never handles a password, because a password passed through a chat or an MCP client is in a transcript. Requires the 'wifi-connect-enabled' consent key. (arguments: ssid)

negatives.desc: list_wifi_networks: Scan for and list the WiFi networks in range, with signal strength and whether this machine is joined to one. Scans the radio, so it requires the 'network-sense-enabled' consent. (arguments: rescan)

toggle_wifi: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off (only Wi-Fi - airplane_mode switches every radio, connect_wifi joins a network), or report whether Wi-Fi is on. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key; status needs no permission. (arguments: action)

solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)
lab_network_list: List the isolated lab networks built on this machine, with their subnets. Read-only.

lab_network_create: Build an isolated lab network on this machine: a network namespace holding a bridge, with named subnets in namespaces of their own. A public subnet can reach the internet through the uplink; a private one can reach this network and nothing beyond it. Returns the exact plan and changes nothing unless apply=true, which needs your system password. (arguments: name, cidr, subnets, internet, apply)
lab_network_destroy: Remove a lab network built by lab_network_create, and everything in it. Only ever removes networks this tool built. Returns the plan unless apply=true. (arguments: name, apply)
lab_network_status: What a lab network can actually reach: a real ping from inside each subnet, not just what the routing table says. (arguments: name)

train.say: Which app opens a kind of file, and the default browser.
train.positives_desc: default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

negatives.desc: open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

list_apps: List the applications installed on this machine, optionally filtered by a search term, so a request to open something can be answered with what actually exists rather than a guess. (arguments: search)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

open_files: Find which programs have a file, directory or network socket open. Use for 'what is using this file', 'why can't I delete this', 'what has my disk open', 'which process is holding that socket'. Names the holding program with its full command line, and flags deleted files whose space cannot be reclaimed. Reads only this user's processes unless run as root. Read-only: it lists open handles and never closes one. (arguments: path, pid, limit)

train.say: Explain a command.
train.positives_desc: explain_command: Explain a Linux shell command (not a general topic) from the local manuals (tldr, man), e.g. 'what does tar do', 'how do I use rsync'; or find which command does something, e.g. 'which command shows disk usage'. (arguments: command, task)

negatives.desc: find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

container: Run containers on this machine with podman (run an image, run a command inside a running container, stop it, read its logs, list what is running, list local images, pull one) and start/stop nspawn machines with machinectl. A container started with display=x11 draws on this desktop, and the ui_elements tool is what drives it by name with a visible cursor; this tool starts it, and stops it. Needs 'container-control-enabled', off by default. (arguments: action, image, name, command, detach, display, share_bus, publish, all, tail)

dissect_traffic: Capture traffic on an interface and dissect it into protocol fields with tshark, Wireshark's command-line engine: which protocols are actually on the wire, and for a filter, the specific fields - TLS handshake type and SNI, DNS query names, HTTP host. This is the companion to capture_packets: that one reads packets as they cross, this one says what they are. Filters use the same grammar as both tools. Reads packet contents, so it needs the same permission as capture_packets. Writes nothing to disk. (arguments: interface, filter, packets, seconds)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

list_processes: List the processes running on this machine, with their pid, name, owner, CPU and memory use, sorted by CPU unless sort_by says otherwise.
